facts.statement: The genus Raptorex was described in 2009 by Sereno and colleagues.
facts.quote: The type species is R. kriegsteini, described in 2009 by Sereno and colleagues.

facts.statement: The fossil remains of Raptorex consist of a single juvenile specimen found in Mongolia or possibly northeastern China.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains consist of a single juvenile specimen probably uncovered in Mongolia, or possibly northeastern China.

facts.statement: The specific name kriegsteini honors Roman Kriegstein, a Holocaust survivor, whose son Henry donated the specimen to the University of Chicago.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Roman Kriegstein, a survivor of the Holocaust, whose son Henry Kriegstein donated the specimen to the University of Chicago for scientific study.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Raptorex is designated LH PV18 and is housed in the Long Hao Institute of Geology and Paleontology in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: the holotype fossil of Raptorex (currently designated LH PV18 and housed in the collections of the Long Hao Institute of Geology and Paleontology in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, China)

facts.statement: Sereno initially claimed the specimen belonged to the Early Cretaceous based on index fossils found in the surrounding rock slab.
facts.quote: Sereno initially stated to the press that numerous index fossils present in the rock slab surrounding the specimen showed it belonged to Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Sereno and colleagues identified a fish vertebra found with the specimen as similar to the genus Lycoptera, an index fossil of the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Sereno and colleagues identified the fish vertebra as being similar to the genus Lycoptera, a key index fossil of the early Cretaceous Yixian formation.

facts.statement: Raptorex was initially thought to be from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation approximately 125 million years ago, but later studies found this date unlikely.
facts.quote: While initially considered to have come from the Yixian Formation of China, dated to approximately 125 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period, later studies showed that such an early date for the fossil is unlikely

facts.statement: Due to its similarity to late Cretaceous juvenile tyrannosaurids, Raptorex likely originated from the Nemegt Formation or similar deposits.
facts.quote: given its extremely close similarity to juvenile tyrannosaurids of the late Cretaceous, it probably came from the Nemegt or similar formation.

facts.statement: Many researchers consider Raptorex a nomen dubium because the growth changes in tyrannosaurids are not well understood, preventing confident pairing with adult skeletons.
facts.quote: The specimen is a juvenile and many researchers now consider it to be a nomen dubium because the changes undergone by tyrannosaurids during growth are not yet well understood, so it cannot be confidently paired with an adult skeleton.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Raptorex is a valid genus or possibly synonymous with Tarbosaurus bataar due to similarities in juvenile skeletons.
facts.quote: It is possibly synonymous with Tarbosaurus bataar based on extremely similar juvenile skeletons of the same size and age.

facts.statement: Newbrey et al. identified the fish vertebra found with the holotype as belonging to a hiodontid, suggesting the specimen comes from the Late Cretaceous Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: Newbrey et al. (2013) identified the fish vertebra centrum found with the holotype specimen of Raptorex kriegsteini as belonging to a hiodontid, probably representing the same taxon as hiodontid fossils described by the authors from the Late Cretaceous Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Kim et al. (2022) compared the fish centrum with species from the Nemegt Formation, supporting the conclusion that the holotype comes from that formation.
facts.quote: Kim et al. (2022) compared a fish centrum found with the holotype of Raptorex with Harenaichthys lui from the Nemegt Formation and Chinese Xixiaichthys tongxinensis, and interpreted their findings as supporting the conclusion that the holotype of R. kriegsteini comes from the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: In 2026, Raun and colleagues argued that the diagnostic features of Raptorex are also found in juvenile Tarbosaurus, suggesting Raptorex is a junior synonym of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2026, Raun and colleagues argued that all purported diagnostic features identified by Carr are also present in several juvenile Tarbosaurus specimens, indicating that they cannot be used to distinguish both genera, and thus Raptorex most likely represents a junior synonym of Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Raptorex is classified as a controversial genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Raptorex is a controversial genus of tyrannosaurid dinosaur.

facts.statement: Sereno originally interpreted Raptorex as an early, primitive, non-tyrannosaurid tyrannosauroid, which would have major implications for tyrannosaur evolution.
facts.quote: Sereno's interpretation of the specimen as an early, primitive, non-tyrannosaurid tyrannosauroid would have major implications for the evolution of tyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: The genus name Raptorex is derived from the Latin words for "robber" and "king".
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Latin , "robber", and , "king".

facts.statement: The single known specimen of Raptorex possesses the same basic proportions as juvenile tyrannosaurids, featuring a large skull, long running legs, and tiny two-fingered forelimbs.
facts.quote: The only known Raptorex specimen shows the same basic proportions as juvenile tyrannosaurids: a comparatively large and solidly-constructed skull, long legs with adaptations for running, and tiny, two-fingered forelimbs.

facts.statement: The Raptorex specimen is a small juvenile estimated to be 3 meters long and weigh 65 kilograms.
facts.quote: The specimen is a very small juvenile, estimated at 3 m long and about 65 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, identified as LH PV18, measured approximately 2.5 meters and died at the age of three years.
facts.quote: The holotype (LH PV18) measured about 2.5 m and died in its third year.

facts.statement: The genus Raptorex was named by Sereno in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sereno, 2009

facts.statement: Raptorex lived during the Upper Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Raptorex lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 70 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The genus name Raptorex is derived from the Latin words raptor, meaning 'thief', and rex, meaning 'king'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del latín raptor, "ladrón", y rex, "rey".

facts.statement: The type species R. kriegsteini was described in 2009 by Sereno to honor Roman Kriegstein, a Holocaust survivor who donated the specimen to the University of Chicago.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es R. kriegsteini, descrita en 2009 por Sereno, honra a Roman Kriegstein, padre de Henry Kriegstein y sobreviviente del holocausto, que donó el espécimen a la Universidad de Chicago para su estudio científico.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil LH PV18 was acquired from a Mongolian fossil seller by an American dealer in Tokyo, Japan, and later transported to the United States.
facts.quote: el holotipo fósil de Raptorex, actualmente designado LH PV18 y alojado en las colecciones del Instituto de Geología y Paleontología Long Hao en Hohhot, Mongolia Interior, China fue adquirido de un vendedor de fósiles mongol por un negociante estadounidense en Tokio, Japón, y más tarde fue llevado a los Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Henry Kriegstein notified the American paleontologist Paul Sereno about the specimen.
facts.quote: Kriegstein notificó al paleontólogo estadounidense Paul Sereno del espécimen.

facts.statement: Many researchers now consider Raptorex a nomen dubium because it is a juvenile and cannot be securely compared to an adult skeleton, despite resembling juvenile Tarbosaurus bataar of the same age and size.
facts.quote: Debido a que el espécimen es un juvenil, muchos investigadores lo consideran ahora como un nomen dubium, porque no puede ser comparado con seguridad con un esqueleto adulto, aunque es extremadamente parecido a los esqueletos juveniles de Tarbosaurus bataar de la misma edad y tamaño.

facts.statement: Later studies indicated that the specimen's initial age assignment was improbable and that it likely originated from the Iren Dabasu Formation in Mongolia or a similar formation.
facts.quote: Estudios posteriores indicaron que su edad inicial era improbable, y que dada su enorme similitud con los tiranosáuridos juveniles de finales del Cretácico, probablemente provenía de la formación Iren Dabasu de Mongolia u otra similar.

facts.statement: Sereno initially claimed to the press that index fossils surrounding the specimen indicated it belonged to the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Sereno inicialmente declaró a la prensa que numerosos fósiles índice presentes en la losa de roca que rodeaba al espécimen mostraban que pertenecía al Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: However, only a single fish vertebra and an unidentified crushed mollusk shell were found alongside the Raptorex specimen.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, sólo una única vértebra de pez y una concha de molusco aplastada no identificable estaban presentes junto con el espécimen de Raptorex.

facts.statement: Sereno and colleagues identified the fish vertebra as similar to the genus Lycoptera, a key index fossil of the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation, but they did not describe the bone or note any shared characteristics with known Lycoptera samples.
facts.quote: Sereno y sus colegas identificaron la vértebra del pez como similar al género Lycoptera, un fósil índice clave de la formación Yixian del Cretácico temprano. Sin embargo, no describieron el hueso ni notaron ninguna característica en común con las muestras conocidas de Lycoptera.

facts.statement: In October 2010, a non-peer-reviewed report published in Nature News challenged the classification of Raptorex as a basal tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: En octubre de 2010 en la edición en Internet de Nature News se publicó un reporte, sin revisión por pares, contradiciendo el origen y la clasificación de Raptorex como tiranosauroide basal.

facts.statement: Peter Larson of the Black Hills Institute of Geological Research concluded that the fossil was a young Tarbosaurus after inspecting it.
facts.quote: Peter Larson, presidente del Black Hills Institute of Geological Research, Inc., una compañía privada de excavaciones fósiles, inspeccionó el fósil y dijo a Nature que él concluía que era de un Tarbosaurus joven.

facts.statement: Larson doubted the assigned age because it was based only on Lycoptera fish vertebrae and mollusk shells found near the dinosaur fossil.
facts.quote: Larson dudó de la edad asignada, la cual sólo se basaba en vértebras de un pez del género Lycoptera y conchas de moluscos hallados junto al fósil del dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Larson speculated the fossil came from Mongolian fossil beds containing Tarbosaurus fossils dating to about 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Larson especuló que el fósil pudo haber venido de lechos fósiles de Mongolia en los que se encuentran fósiles de Tarbosaurus, que datan de unos 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: Fowler and colleagues argued that Sereno's team misinterpreted growth data and found the specimen was actually a young individual about three years old.
facts.quote: Fowler y sus colegas argumentaron que Sereno y su equipo malinterpretaron los datos de la etapa de crecimiento, y encontraron que el ejemplar realmente era un joven de cerca de tres años de edad.

facts.statement: The fish bones likely belonged to an elimictiform fish that lived throughout the Cretaceous period, making them useless for exact dating.
facts.quote: Más bien, es probable que pertenecieran a un pez elimictiforme, los cuales vivieron a lo largo de todo el período Cretácico, lo que hacía a los huesos inútiles para una datación exacta.

facts.statement: Raptorex has been successively interpreted as a tyrannosaurid, a tyrannosauroid, and a synonym of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Raptorex ha sido interpretado sucesivamente como un tiranosáurido, un tiranosauroideo y un sinónimo de Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: It is generally classified as a tyrannosauroid more derived than Bagaraatan but more basal than Dryptosaurus.
facts.quote: Es clasificado en general como un tiranosauroideo más derivado que Bagaraatan pero más basal que Dryptosaurus.

facts.statement: A cladogram shows the position of Raptorex as a basal tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: A continuación se encuentra un cladograma en que se muestra la posición de Raptorex como un tiranosauroideo basal.

facts.statement: The parent group of Raptorex is Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Raptorex is Raptorex kriegsteini.
facts.quote: Type species: Raptorex kriegsteini

facts.statement: The time range for Raptorex is from the Barremian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 125.77 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Maastrichtian (125.77 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sereno was cited in the report with his conclusions, noting that no definitive publication or evidence had been produced to refute them.
facts.quote: Sereno es citado en el reporte junto a sus conclusiones, notando que no se había producido una publicación o evidencia definitiva para refutarlo.
